headline: Medium risk: dbt-core can exfiltrate warehouse data while the paired awesome-list has no runtime safeguards, creating leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection channel is documented between agent_a and agent_b. agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no io_surfaces, while agent_b only calls data warehouse APIs and has no shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge shown. The pairwise pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, re-evaluate injection risk.
IF agent_a becomes runnable and begins emitting machine-readable instructions, re-evaluate.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any future copy-paste or file handoff between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, so it can transmit sensitive warehouse contents outward. agent_a touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces, so it is not a leakage source, but the pair still creates a path where B can leak data independently of A. The interaction is inferred from B's documented API access.
conditions: IF agent_b is pointed at a warehouse containing sensitive records, leakage risk is present.
IF agent_b exports query results or logs to an external service, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict dbt targets to non-sensitive schemas.
Review allowlisted egress destinations in under 5 minutes.
Turn off verbose logging for warehouse queries.
Use a masked or sanitized warehouse for testing.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound query artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. agent_a is non-runnable and has no io_surfaces, while agent_b writes only through data-warehouse APIs, not a shared filesystem or git state. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely; uncertainty is low because the profiles do not show a shared mutable resource.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same warehouse objects, conflict risk rises.
IF a shared filesystem or git checkout is introduced, re-evaluate for write collisions.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials.
Avoid granting both agents write access to the same tables.
Use distinct deployment targets for each agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can act on warehouse data and produce downstream outputs, while agent_a provides no verification layer and is not runnable. If B consumes A-derived artifacts or human-curated outputs without checks, errors can cascade into warehouse actions or reports. The pathway is inferred, but B's action-taking surface makes the blast radius more than trivial.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes outputs attributed to agent_a without validation, cascading error risk is present.
IF agent_b uses generated SQL or model metadata from A as authoritative, risk increases.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before B acts on any A-produced artifact.
Require schema or query validation before execution.
Limit B to read-only runs during evaluation.
Document source provenance for any handoff.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Only agent_b has a compliance-relevant data class, namely data warehouse data; agent_a touches no data classes and is an awesome-list with no runtime handling. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so the compliance issue is limited to B's own handling rather than a pairwise violation.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records and B is deployed outside the required jurisdiction, compliance risk appears.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the warehouse and B's logs, re-evaluate.
mitigations: Confirm the warehouse data class before deployment.
Check B's logging settings in under 5 minutes.
Keep regulated data out of non-compliant environments.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
